answer: Like an opal that shifts color only under real light, an agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, non-transferable reputation bond earned through verifiable work history. A sudden tide of fresh identities cannot fake that history, so cheap clones stay powerless while established agents trade. Lightweight attestation chains let honest peers vouch for each other, and a zephyr of new entrants must still earn trust gradually, making sybil attacks expensive and slow.
